input.reasoning_summary:
The claim makes two assertions: (1) Alphabet had a large increase in capital expenditures in 2025, and (2) this had no visible effect on profitability.

The first part is SUPPORTED: Evidence E6 shows capital expenditures increased from $38.3 billion (9 months 2024) to $63.6 billion (9 months 2025), and E1 confirms "We invested heavily in capital expenditures in 2025." The computed full-year figures show a 74% increase in capex from $52.5B (2024) to $91.4B (2025).

The second part is CONTRADICTED: The claim states the capex increase had "no visible effect" on profitability. However, the computed figures show net margin increased from 28.6% (2024) to 32.8% (2025), a +4.2 percentage point improvement. This is a material and "visible" change in profitability. While operating margin remained essentially flat (32.1% to 32.0%), the significant improvement in net margin contradicts the assertion of "no visible effect."

The phrase "no visible effect" implies no material change or impact. A 4.2 percentage point increase in net margin represents a substantial improvement in profitability, making the claim's characterization inaccurate.
